Earlier there had been rumours that Apple is developing a brand-new all-glass iPhone to mark its 20th anniversary next year. However, Jefferies analysts believe that development work on the device has come to a halt.

Wall Street analysts say the major redesign plan for the 20th anniversary iPhone has been cancelled

Wall Street investment bank Jefferies today downgraded Apple's stock rating to "Underperform", with analyst Edison Lee pointing out that the possible cancellation of the major redesign for the 20th anniversary iPhone is one of the main reasons.

The key to this downgrade lies in the suspected cancellation of Apple's all-glass iPhone. Although reports as early as 2025 indicated that the project was under development, and there were rumours that it would debut as early as 2027, Apple has never responded to such speculation. However, Apple had quietly filed a patent for a "six-sided glass enclosure" as early as 2019. Jefferies had previously thought there was a chance an all-glass iPhone could launch, but Lee believes development work has ground to a halt. He indicated that supply chain checks showed the project was cancelled due to low yield rates. Lee considers this decision "a major setback for driving higher iPhone pricing at a time when memory costs are soaring". If the device does launch in September 2027 to mark the iPhone's 20th anniversary, the estimated average retail price would reach US$2,060, higher than the average selling price of any previous model. Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe the original plan was to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, further raising their average selling prices and gross margins." He believes that, with memory prices continuing to climb, this would have been an important defensive strategy.

Lee also pointed out that Apple's AI strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro are reasons for the further downgrade of the company's stock rating.

From Lee's report, it is difficult to determine whether the analyst believes the entire redesign plan has been shelved, or only some design elements have been cancelled.

For example, speculation circulating in the market suggests Apple may not be able to completely remove the Dynamic Island cutout next year. As a result, an "all-glass" display will not be possible. However, the rumoured four-sided curved design could still potentially launch.

In any case, if Apple's iPhone 20th anniversary design plan really has been cancelled, other reliable sources should soon confirm it.

What are your thoughts on this report about the iPhone 20th anniversary design? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
